skill.name: pixijs-html-source
skill.description: Use this skill when rendering live HTML/DOM elements (or frozen snapshots of them) as PixiJS v8 textures via the EXPERIMENTAL HTML-in-Canvas browser APIs. Covers the pixi.js/html-source import, feature detection with canvas.requestPaint, HTMLSource for a live, repainting, still-interactive element (autoLayout/autoUpdate/autoRequestPaint, requestPaint, isReady, HTMLSource.defaultOptions, the direct-child-of-canvas + layoutsubtree requirement), ElementImageSource for an immutable captureElementImage() snapshot (autoClose, ready immediately), using the source on a Sprite/Texture/Mesh, fallback-only auto-detection via Texture.from at priority -10, uploader error messages, and destroy/cleanup. Triggers on: HTMLSource, ElementImageSource, ElementImage, HTML in canvas, render DOM to texture, render HTML to texture, texElementImage2D, copyElementImageToTexture, HTMLSourceOptions, ElementImageSourceOptions, HTMLSourceCanvas.
skill.summary: Render live DOM elements or immutable HTML snapshots as PixiJS v8 textures using experimental browser APIs.
skill.author: pixijs

content.value_statement: Rendering live HTML inside GPU scenes requires experimental browser APIs and careful texture lifecycle management. This skill guides PixiJS v8 integrations using live DOM sources or immutable element snapshots.
actual_capabilities: Explain pixi.js/html-source imports and registration of WebGL and WebGPU texture uploaders.
Guide live HTMLSource setup with canvas ownership, layoutsubtree, paint events, and readiness checks.
Demonstrate requestPaint scheduling for continuously changing DOM content.
Explain immutable ElementImageSource snapshots, autoClose ownership, and explicit cleanup.
Show texture framing, sprite conversion, mesh mapping, and fallback source detection at priority -10.
Identify missing browser API errors and suggest static image or DOM overlay fallbacks.
limitations: Requires experimental HTML-in-Canvas browser APIs that may need a browser flag and may change between minor releases.
DOM capture is unavailable in Web Workers.
Live HTMLSource elements require the owning canvas layout subtree and direct-child placement.
Provides documentation and examples, not a bundled renderer, compatibility polyfill, or automated test suite.

use_cases.target_user: Frontend developers building experimental canvas interfaces

prompt_templates.title: Start With a Live Element
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a minimal PixiJS v8 HTMLSource example for an editable input. Include feature detection, canvas child placement, and the correct imports.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a first live HTML texture

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Frozen Snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ElementImageSource from my existing canvas child. Explain readiness, exclusive snapshot ownership, and cleanup when the sprite is removed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: reuse a fixed element appearance

prompt_templates.title: Debug Repaint Scheduling
prompt_templates.prompt: My HTMLSource clock texture stops updating. Review autoUpdate, autoRequestPaint, paint events, and ticker scheduling, then recommend a repaint lifecycle with cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Shared Snapshot Effect
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PixiJS v8 effect using one ElementImage across multiple sources and mesh textures. Address ownership, framing, unsupported-browser fallbacks, and final cleanup.

output_examples.input: Why does my HTMLSource texture fail on its first render?
output: Check whether canvas.requestPaint exists before creating the HTML texture.
Import HTMLSource from pixi.js/html-source to register the required uploaders.
If the experimental API is unavailable, choose a static image or DOM overlay fallback.

output_examples.input: Can two ElementImageSource instances share a snapshot?
output: Yes. Leave autoClose disabled while multiple sources share the snapshot.
Destroy each source after its final use.
Close the shared snapshot once after every consumer has finished.

output_examples.input: How should a clock rendered through HTMLSource keep updating?
output: Place the clock element directly under the owning canvas.
Update its text in the application ticker and request a paint each frame.
Remove the ticker callback and destroy the source when the clock is no longer needed.

best_practices: Feature-detect experimental browser APIs and provide a fallback before relying on HTML textures.
Import from pixi.js/html-source and attach live elements to the owning canvas before source construction.
Assign snapshot ownership explicitly, remove application ticker callbacks, and destroy sources after their final use.
anti_patterns: Importing HTMLSource from the core pixi.js entry instead of pixi.js/html-source.
Expecting continuously changing DOM content to repaint without explicit requestPaint scheduling.
Enabling autoClose on a snapshot that remains shared with other sources.

faq.question: Which PixiJS version does this skill address?
faq.answer: It addresses experimental HTMLSource and ElementImageSource APIs in PixiJS v8.

faq.question: Does HTML-in-Canvas work in every browser?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes experimental APIs behind a browser flag. Detect canvas.requestPaint and provide a fallback.

faq.question: What is the difference between HTMLSource and ElementImageSource?
faq.answer: HTMLSource tracks a live DOM element through paint events. ElementImageSource wraps an immutable snapshot that never repaints.

faq.question: Where should I import these texture sources?
faq.answer: Import them from pixi.js/html-source. This entry registers their source extensions and WebGL and WebGPU uploaders.

faq.question: Can I capture DOM elements in a Web Worker?
faq.answer: No. Web Workers have no DOM, so these capture workflows require a browser context with DOM access.

faq.question: When should I enable autoClose?
faq.answer: Enable it only when one source exclusively owns the snapshot. For shared snapshots, close manually after the final consumer finishes.
